findings.current: “Gate transformations were rare even during the Great Cataclysm. For one to occur, an extremely powerful monster had to take center stage and sink its mana into the area.”
findings.defect: “Take center stage” loses the mechanical explanation that the monster must serve as the phenomenon’s core, while “sink its mana” does not clearly preserve the image of mana taking root.
findings.rationale: 주축이 되다 means to become the central axis or core, and 마력을 뿌리내리다 describes establishing or rooting mana in the location.
findings.replacement: “Gate transformations were rare even during the Great Cataclysm. For one to occur, an extremely powerful monster had to serve as its core and anchor its mana in the area.”
findings.source: “게이트화는 대격변 때도 드문 현상이었지. 그러기 위해서는 매우 강력한 몬스터가 주축이 되어 마력을 뿌리내려야 하니 말일세.”

findings.current: Humanity would undoubtedly be the final victor, but countless cities would be destroyed, and tens—or perhaps hundreds—of millions of people would die.
findings.defect: The draft incorrectly applies “millions” to both numerical terms, inflating the projected deaths from hundreds of thousands or millions to tens or hundreds of millions.
findings.rationale: 수십 in this escalating construction elides 만 before the correction to 수백만, yielding hundreds of thousands followed by perhaps millions, not tens or hundreds of millions.
findings.replacement: Humanity would undoubtedly emerge victorious in the end, but countless cities would be destroyed, and hundreds of thousands—no, perhaps millions—of people would die.
findings.source: 분명 최후의 승자는 인간이 되겠지만, 수많은 도시가 파괴되고 수십, 아니 어쩌면 수백만 이상의 사람들이 죽을 것이다.

findings.current: “Do you suspect me and my friend as well?”
findings.defect: The possessive “my friend” invents a friendly relationship between Lee Jungryong and Wu Heixing and removes Lee’s distancing reference to “that fellow.”
findings.rationale: 저 친구 refers deictically to Wu Heixing as “that fellow”; it does not identify him as Lee’s friend.
findings.replacement: “Do you suspect me and that fellow too?”

findings.defect: Leaving the Korean-derived intensifier “Jonna” unexplained produces meaningless English and loses the Formation J punchline.
findings.rationale: The line reveals that Formation J amounts to “Just fucking fight,” preserving the crude joke and the significance of the letter J.

findings.current: “I’m certain that these fucking bastards are more interested in stabbing me in the back than in the Arch Lich.”
findings.defect: The draft turns the source’s indirect, darkly comic reference to the back of Taekyung’s head into an explicit statement that they intend to betray him.
findings.rationale: 내 뒤통수에 더 관심이 있다 alludes to being struck or betrayed without explicitly saying “stab me in the back,” and 뭐 그런 확신이요 supplies a separate deadpan qualification.
findings.replacement: “These fucking bastards are more interested in the back of my head than the Arch Lich. That’s what I’m certain of.”
findings.source: “이 씨벌 새끼들이 아크 리치보다는 내 뒤통수에 더 관심이 있구나. 뭐 그런 확신이요.”

findings.defect: The established term 일격 is replaced with the generic lowercase phrase “final strike.”
findings.rationale: The binding glossary establishes 일격 as “One Strike,” while 끝을 알리는 describes the blow as signaling the end.
findings.replacement: A lightning-fast One Strike that signaled the end.

findings.current: Lee Jungryong looked around with sunken eyes before finally speaking.
findings.defect: “Sunken eyes” describes a physical, haggard appearance rather than the subdued or grave quality of Lee Jungryong’s gaze.
findings.rationale: 가라앉은 modifies the mood of his gaze, not the physical position or condition of his eyes.
findings.replacement: Lee Jungryong swept his surroundings with a somber gaze, then spoke.
findings.source: 가라앉은 눈빛으로 주위를 둘러보던 이정룡이 입술을 뗐다.

summary: One critical quantity error, with additional losses in the Gate mechanism, character relationships, humor, euphemism, terminology, and natural description.
